analyzed_vuln.description: Heap buffer overflow in the bundled zstd decoder: ZSTD_execSequenceEnd() calls ZSTD_safecopy() for literals/matches near block end, and ZSTD_safecopy() may write up to WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH (16) bytes past oend_w by design. In this PoV, the decoded sequence lengths are inconsistent with the small destination chunk size, and the end-of-block copy loop in ZSTD_safecopy (line ~753) writes past the allocated output buffer (ASan shows write 2 bytes past a 176-byte heap region). The crash is in safecopy, but root cause is accepting/processing malformed sequence data such that execSequenceEnd performs an out-of-bounds tail copy.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Data flow: fuzz_decompress_frame.c -> frame/schunk lazy chunk path -> blosc2_getitem/_blosc_getitem -> blosc_d -> zstd_wrap_decompress -> ZSTD_decompressFrame -> ZSTD_decompressBlock_internal -> ZSTD_decompressSequences -> ZSTD_execSequenceEnd. The PoV crafts a Blosc frame containing a zstd-compressed block whose sequence stream yields a final sequence copied in the slow end-path. Trigger requires malformed zstd sequence/literal/match lengths that pass earlier checks but drive ZSTD_safecopy tail handling to write beyond the provided dst buffer for that chunk.
